input.question: With advances in immunology and medicine, how has our immune system changed over the last hundred years?
input.ground_truth: 100 years is effectively zero time in evolutionary terms for a species with our generation time, unless the selective pressure is ludicrously high (e.g. selective breeding where all the offspring that don't have the desired trait get their necks snapped by the breeder). For more 'normal' environmental pressures, you're looking at tens of thousands of years to see something spread across the population.

Question: With advances in immunology and medicine, how has our immune system changed over the last hundred years?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your body is like a castle, and the soldiers inside are your immune system. They help keep you safe from germs, like tiny bad guys.

A hundred years ago, the soldiers didn’t have very good tools or maps to find the bad guys. Sometimes, they got sick or tired, and it was hard to fix you when you got really sick.

But now, scientists (like smart wizards) have given the soldiers better tools, like tiny shields and super maps. They also found medicines that help the soldiers fight the bad guys even better. Because of this, your castle (your body) is much safer now, and the soldiers can help you get better faster when you’re sick.

So, our immune system soldiers are still the same, but now they have better help to keep us healthy! 🛡️🧪👑
